events.objective: Establish the real onset time and blast radius of the settlement stall. Query logs and metrics for settlement-service and its topic: when did consumer lag start climbing vs. when did processed-settlement throughput drop to zero (was there a slow ramp or a hard stop)? Identify error/exception signatures in settlement-service logs and whether they point upstream (fetch/publish errors, rebalance storms, connection resets) or downstream (DB timeouts, RPC failures). Also check current CPU/memory/GC/thread/resource trends on settlement-service pods and broker/queue health metrics to rule in/out resource exhaustion or broker instability. Report exact timestamps and the dominant error signatures.

Enumerate everything that changed across ALL services in the window 2026-05-12T06:00Z to now, not just settlement-service: deployments, config changes, feature flags. Specifically characterize the reported consumer poll-settings change (exact time, which instances/services, values old vs new). Map settlement-service's dependencies and dependents (get_service_dependencies) to identify shared components — message broker/topic, ledger/posting service, DB — and which upstream producers feed the settlements topic. Note any change in that window to upstream producers or shared broker config. Also search_historical_incidents for prior settlement lag / consumer stall incidents and their root causes.

Correlate the change timeline against the true onset from task a: using the exact change timestamps and any non-settlement changes reported by task b, determine which event's time lines up with the first sign of trouble. Check whether lag growth began before the poll-settings change (implying an upstream/shared-component cause) and whether topic-level producer metrics (publish rate, produce errors, partition skew) or downstream call latency from settlement-service degraded at onset. Output a ranked statement of which signal moved first.

args.query: settlement consumer lag stuck messages not processed

events.statement: The only config change across all services in the window was on settlement-service: consumer.max.poll.records reduced from 500 to 200 at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z (author m.das, reason 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes').

The only deployment across all services in the window was order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan), which renamed the OrderExecuted event field qty -> quantity, added field 'venue', and added an event schema version header v2; status live, not rolled back.
settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka broker (queue-consume) and reads/writes the shared ledger-db (postgres, owner platform); both are shared components used by multiple services.

Upstream producers feeding the shared kafka broker are order-service (queue-produce) and payment-service (queue-produce); settlement-service and notification-service both consume from the same broker, so a broker-side rebalance would affect both consumers.

ledger-db is shared by four writers: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all have db edges to ledger-db, so a change or load in any of those can affect settlement posting through the shared DB.
No config changes were found for the shared kafka broker in the window (count 0).

Prior settlement-lag precedent: HIST-112 (2026-02-03) 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' — lag growing, settlements stuck, root cause 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance', resolved by restarting the consumer group; HIST-104 describes a Kafka broker rebalance storm causing consumer lag.

Timeline note: the settlement-service poll-settings change (07:35Z) precedes the order-service v2 schema deployment (07:40Z) by 5 minutes; both sit ~47 min before the 08:22Z report, so neither is immediately adjacent to the reported onset.

events.description: No metrics were pulled for kafka, ledger-db, order-service or settlement-service (consumer lag, broker partition/rebalance events, DB load), so the exact onset time and whether the failure is produce-side (order-service v2 events) or consume-side (poll setting) could not be confirmed.

get_config_changes was queried per-service only for kafka; feature-flag changes (as opposed to config changes) across other services were not separately enumerated, and the 'all services' config query returned only one change, so any flag-specific store was not inspected.

search_historical_incidents returned only 5 results (match scores 4,2,1,1,1) and did not surface incidents tied specifically to poll-settings or producer schema-version changes; no free-text date filter was applied.

events.answer: Across ALL services in the 2026-05-12T06:00Z–09:59Z window, only two changes exist: a settlement-service config change (cfg-3004: consumer.max.poll.records 500 → 200 at 07:35Z, author m.das) and a single deployment (dep-6010: order-service v2.16.0 "Order events v2" at 07:40Z, which renames the OrderExecuted field qty→quantity and adds a schema-version header). order-service is an upstream producer to the shared kafka broker that settlement-service consumes from, and it also writes to the shared ledger-db — so both the reported consumer change and the upstream producer schema change are candidates. There were no changes to the shared kafka broker or ledger-db config in the window.

events.statement: Consumer lag on settlement-service switches from a flat baseline of ~38-55 messages to sustained growth at the 07:41 bucket: 07:39 bucket avg 37.78/max 39.7 → 07:41 avg 206.44/max 386.63 → 07:43 avg 1063.21 → 07:49 avg 3688.8/max 3865.43, reaching avg 60412.45/max 61605.53 by 09:56. This is a hard departure from baseline, not a gradual pre-existing trend.

Throughput stopped essentially in the same bucket as the lag onset: request_rate was ~61-63 req/s through the 07:32 bucket, fell to avg 16.32 in the 07:40 bucket, and was down to avg 0.41/max 0.44 by the 07:48 bucket where it stayed flat (~0.40-0.41) for the rest of the window — i.e. zero settlements processed within ~2 minutes of the first deserialization error, not a long slow ramp.

Dominant error signature in settlement-service logs is a deserialization/schema failure, first at 2026-05-12T07:42:14Z and repeated 213 times through 09:58:31Z: "failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)" — the same offset orders-3@8841207 recurs in every occurrence.

The error escalates into a poison-message retry loop on the same partition from 2026-05-12T07:44:51Z (196 occurrences, attempts in the tens of thousands, e.g. attempt 92490): "poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt 92490), partition blocked" — i.e. the stuck offset blocks partition 3 consumption.

All 409 matched log records in 07:00-09:59 were ERROR level, and the only two patterns are the deserialization failure and the poison-message/partition-blocked retry. No fetch/publish errors, rebalance storms, connection resets, DB timeouts or RPC failures appear in the settlement-service error stream.

settlement-service pod/resource metrics show no exhaustion signal: cpu_pct went 27.48 (07:32 bucket) to ~58.26 (07:40) then held ~68-71 flat to the end (max 78.28); memory_pct stayed ~49-51 flat; db_pool_in_use ~5.8-6.2 flat (max 6.78); restarts 0.0 for the entire window.

The lag onset (~07:41 bucket) follows the reported consumer poll-setting change and precedes the first logged error (07:42:14Z) by about a minute; the first error is the schema mismatch on orders-3@8841207, and the poison/partition-blocked loop starts 07:44:51Z. The stall is upstream-inbound (an unprocessable inbound orders topic record), not a resource or broker-side fault visible on settlement-service.

events.description: Broker/queue health metrics (topic partition status, broker CPU/IO, under-replicated partitions, ISR, request errors) were never queried — the task's tool-call budget was exhausted after the settlement-service log/metric queries.
No log query at INFO level for the pre-onset window (07:35-07:50) completed — that call returned budget_exhausted; only WARN+ (all ERROR) logs from 07:00 onward were retrieved.
Neighbouring services (orders producer / other consumers of the orders topic) were not queried for the same schema/symptom.
Settlement-service log retrieval was truncated (returned 40 of 409 matches, truncated:true).

events.answer: The settlement stall is a hard stop, not a slow ramp: consumer lag on settlement-service was flat (~40-55 msgs) until the 07:41 bucket, then climbed monotonically to ~60.6k by 09:56, while settlement request_rate collapsed from ~62/s to ~0.4/s within the same bucket (07:40-07:48). The dominant signature is a schema/data error repeatedly failing to deserialize orders-3@8841207 ("missing required field 'qty'", header says v2 vs expected v1) from 07:42:14Z onward, escalating to "poison message ... partition blocked" from 07:44:51Z — no fetch/publish, rebalance, connection-reset, DB-timeout or RPC error signatures appear. Pod health looks normal (CPU ~27%→~70% and flat, memory ~50% flat, db_pool_in_use ~6 flat, restarts 0), which argues against resource exhaustion on settlement-service, but I could not query the broker/queue metrics (budget exhausted) so broker instability is not ruled in or out from my data.

events.statement: Coarse 11-minute buckets make the lag onset and the order-service deploy look simultaneous, but at this resolution the poll-settings change at 07:35Z has no accompanying signal: order-service request_rate is flat across the change (07:36 bucket avg 230.97, 07:47 avg 231.53, vs 06:30 avg 225.64; window mean 231.5, min 197.21 max 256.25, missing_points 0), and settlement throughput collapse appears only in the 07:40-07:48 buckets — consistent with the 07:40Z deploy, not the 07:35Z config change.

Upstream producer order-service shows no degradation at onset: error_rate is flat and negligible for the whole window (07:25 avg 0.22, 07:36 avg 0.21, 07:47 avg 0.2, 07:58 avg 0.22; min 0.1 max 0.32, mean 0.22) — no produce-error or publish-failure signature appears, so there is no evidence of upstream topic-level producer failure.

Downstream call latency from settlement-service did NOT degrade at onset: latency_p99_ms is flat across the stall (07:36 avg 243.6, 07:48 avg 238.79, 08:00 avg 239.16, 09:48 avg 237.22; mean 238.27, missing_points 0) — no DB-timeout/RPC-failure latency signature, so downstream latency is not the first mover.

The other upstream producer to the shared broker, payment-service, is healthy at onset: request_rate flat (07:40 avg 99.78, 07:54 avg 99.36, mean 99.96, missing_points 0) and latency_p99_ms flat (07:40 avg 320.82, 07:54 avg 322.63, mean 319.73). payment-service therefore did not change its publish behaviour at 07:40Z.

The other consumer of the same shared broker, notification-service, shows no symptom at onset — a broker-side rebalance/common-component cause would be expected to affect it too, but its error_rate is flat through the window (07:26 avg 0.23, 07:40 avg 0.19, 07:54 avg 0.2, mean 0.21, missing_points 0), so broker-wide consumer disruption is not supported.

No settlement-service WARN/ERROR log lines with 'lag' and no order-service log lines containing 'quantity' were retrievable in the onset window (both queries returned 0 matches against data_range 04:00-09:59Z), so the producer-side view of the schema change and any consumer-rebalance warning could not be directly confirmed.

events.description: No broker/queue component metrics (topic-level publish rate/publish offset rate, produce errors, per-partition skew, consumer group rebalance count) could be queried — my budget was exhausted after service-level metrics, and T1 reported the same limitation. Available_metrics exposed only service-level names for the services I queried; no queue/broker component was queried directly.

order-service application logs returned 0 matches for 'quantity' in 07:35-08:30Z (data_range 04:00-09:59Z), and settlement-service logs for 'lag' returned 0 matches — so I could not verify the producer-side emission of v2 events or a consumer rebalance/reconnect warning at onset.

Metric buckets on order-service (660s) and payment-service/notification-service (840s) are coarser than the 07:35-07:42 minute-level ordering I needed, and finer-grained data was not available via max_points tuning within budget.

events.answer: Ranking of what moved first: (1) order-service v2.16.0 deploy at 07:40Z (qty→quantity field rename + v2 schema header) — the first sign of trouble, the settlement-service deserialization failure on orders-3@8841207 ("missing required field 'qty'", header v2 vs expected v1), starts at 07:42:14Z, ~2 min after the deploy and ~7 min after the poll-setting change; (2) the consumer lag/throughput collapse in the 07:40-07:41 buckets; (3) the poison-message/partition-blocked loop at 07:44:51Z. The 07:35Z consumer.max.poll.records change is not aligned with onset: no settlement signal degraded in the 07:35-07:40 window, and lag growth did NOT begin before the poll-settings change. Upstream producer health and downstream/settlement latency are flat, so neither topic-level producer degradation nor downstream call latency explains the onset.
